first_impression.reaction: I searched 'santorini wedding packages' because every Santorini PDF calls itself a package and means something different. First line: 'Santorini wedding packages share a name and very little else.' Good. No sunsets-and-paradise opener, just the problem, then the actual list of where they differ: rooms, sole use, food, late finishes, suppliers. That's my worry list. Kept reading.

journey.quote: Several Santorini venues require a wedding planner on top of the venue fee, which changes what a package is really worth to you.
journey.reaction: I didn't know that, and it's exactly the kind of thing that turns into a second invoice. Honest trade-off, up front. Good.

journey.section: Ceremony space, set-up and a coordinator
journey.quote: The Panorama Balcony and Caldera Arches package at Canaves Oia Suites is a ceremony and dinner reception for up to 30 guests.
journey.reaction: Up to 30. Then 40 at the Veranda, then 'Santorini suits a small wedding'. We're 60 to 90. For the first half of the piece I was starting to think Santorini just isn't built for a wedding our size.

journey.section: Ceremony space, set-up and a coordinator
journey.quote: Each includes the altar table, chandelier, lanterns with candles, Tiffany chairs, a sound system, round or rectangular tables, linen, plating, cutlery, accessible facilities, an air-conditioned bridal room, in-house catering facilities and a bar.
journey.reaction: This is where I started skimming. A long inventory of chairs and cutlery doesn't help me decide anything. Tell me what's different, not everything.

journey.section: Reception, menus and drinks where the venue states them
journey.quote: Open bar packages are optional, but once chosen they apply to every adult guest.
journey.reaction: That's a hidden-cost line I'd have missed. With 80 guests that's a real number. Useful.

journey.section: Reception, menus and drinks where the venue states them
journey.quote: The Andronis package itself adds floral decor for the ceremony, a bridal bouquet and boutonniere, a two-tier wedding cake, a bottle of sparkling wine with chocolate-covered strawberries, a private cliffside ceremony area, Andronis Heart koufeta favours, a symbolic gift and a romantic turndown with sparkling wine and strawberries.
journey.reaction: Chocolate strawberries and a romantic turndown is exactly the resort-package feel we don't want. Not the article's fault, it's the venue's list, but it confirms a venue package alone won't feel like us.

journey.quote: At Canaves Epitome, the room requirement grows with the guest list: one room for three nights for 8 to 25 guests, three rooms for 26 to 45, then four or six rooms, a half buyout of 25 rooms for 80 to 100 guests and a full buyout of 53 rooms above 100, each with a three-night minimum.
journey.reaction: Finally a number that fits us: 80 to 100 means a half buyout. That's the kind of condition you only learn on the third email with a venue. This section is the most useful part of the piece.

journey.quote: Santorini Gem sets clear rules: the venue provides its standard set-up, set-up starts from 1pm on the day, there is no storage, and confetti, plate smashing and flying lanterns are not permitted.
journey.reaction: Insider detail. No storage and a 1pm set-up start matter to whoever's running the day. Reads like someone actually read the fine print.

journey.section: Venue package, venue fee or a planner
journey.quote: A planner connects the venue, suppliers and guests into one plan, and is the route several Santorini venues insist on.
journey.reaction: Fair and not pushy. I'd still want to know what 'connects' means in practice for us, but the trade-off list itself is honest.

journey.section: How to compare two Santorini quotes like for like
journey.quote: Weather plan. What is the covered or indoor alternative if the wind rises, and is it held for you or offered on the day?
journey.reaction: Wind on the caldera, and 'held for you or offered on the day'. That's a question from someone who's seen it go wrong. The step-free access one right below it is the grandparents question. This checklist goes to James tonight.

journey.section: For Australian couples: currency, deposits and insurance
journey.quote: How much does the exchange rate move the total between the deposit and the balance, and who carries that risk?
journey.reaction: Currency surprise is my number one fear and this names it properly. Mum and Dad are paying 40 percent, so they'll want this list too.

journey.section: For Australian couples: currency, deposits and insurance
journey.quote: It notes that Greece is in an active seismic zone, including near Santorini, and that wildfires occur in the extended summer period from June to September.
journey.reaction: Not romantic, but my dad will ask, and I'd rather hear it here than after the deposit. Builds trust.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit, so you can [book a Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-wedding-packages&utm_content=primary) with both quotes in hand.
journey.reaction: AUD and in writing, yes please. But 'with both quotes in hand' assumes we already have quotes. We haven't even picked a country. And is the Advisor the Concierge, or two different people? Slightly muddled.

unanswered_questions: For 60 to 90 guests with half flying in from Australia, which Santorini venues would you actually shortlist?
Which of these venues can older guests reach without stairs?
Who gets our guests, including grandparents, from the airport or port to the venue?
Who is physically there on the day if something goes wrong: our Wedded Advisor, someone you're accountable for, or the venue's coordinator?
Is there a real Santorini wedding you've planned, with venue and date, that we can look at?
would_share_with: James (partner): the quote comparison checklist, to send the same questions to every venue
Mum and Dad (contributing): the currency, deposit and insurance questions and the seismic and wildfire note
Both sets of parents: the legal section, so they understand the CNI and recognition back home

cta_reaction.quote: When your shortlist is ready, [plan your Santorini wedding with the Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-wedding-packages&utm_content=closing), or return to [our curated Greece wedding collection](https://weddedwonderland.com/destinations/europe/greece).
cta_reaction.why: Calm, not pushy, and the AUD-in-writing promise is a genuine plus. But we're early, with no shortlist and no quotes, and I'd want to see one real wedding and two more posts before handing over our details.

top_3_changes: Help a 60 to 90 guest couple early: the larger options (Grace Hotel over 50, Canaves Epitome 45 to 100 and buyouts, Vedema up to 150) are scattered, so signpost them near the top or in the small-wedding section so Santorini doesn't read as small weddings only.
Cut the long item-by-item inventories (Santorini Gem evening set-up, Andronis inclusions) down to what differs between venues; the comparison is the useful part, not the cutlery.

Reword the primary CTA so it works for couples without quotes yet (drop or soften 'with both quotes in hand'), and make it clear whether the Wedded Advisor and the Wedded Concierge are the same service.

checks.check: Every journey point and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Every turn-off has a why (none found; not invented)
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Sophie (planner_couple), using persona voice and concerns
No invented brand facts; missing details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments and VERIFY markers ignored
Title, business details and absent prices treated as not must-fix; no requests for sourcing or not-published lines

assumptions: Arrived from a Google search for 'santorini wedding packages' during early destination research, about 14 months out.
Skimmed long venue inventories; read the left-out, quote comparison, legal and Australian sections closely.
No prices appear by design, so the 'vague pricing' turn-off was not raised.
Transfers, on-the-day accountability and real weddings are deferred business details, listed as unanswered questions only and not as must-fix.
Venue-supplied wording (e.g. 'romantic turndown') was not counted as a brand cliché turn-off.
The persona card is provisional (not CRM-calibrated).
